- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, increase forecast downward bias to reflect bearish momentum.  
- When model forecast is rising sharply after a spike, cap the next few days’ forecast growth to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after a spike, price drops back toward prior range), adjust forecast to reflect this.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong volatility or sentiment swings, reduce forecast smoothness to account for noise.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to neutral/negative), adjust forecast to reflect potential correction.  
- Avoid forecasting upward trends when sentiment is flat or mildly negative unless accompanied by strong technical confirmation.
